- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → overconfident upward bias).
- When sentiment is negative (especially >3 consecutive negative values), model underestimates downward moves; apply a 5-10% downward adjustment to forecasted peaks.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 10-20% in next 3-5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10-14 day horizons; if forecast is >15% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5-10%.
- Sentiment history with 2+ consecutive positive values → model overestimates; apply a 5-15% downward correction to avoid “sentiment-driven overreach.”
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to anticipate the drop — add a 5-10% downward bias to forecast for next 5 days.
- Forecast horizon >15 days: model tends to underestimate downward trends — add 3-7% downward bias if sentiment is negative or neutral.
